title: Brian Downey (drummer) - Wikipedia
notes: Brian Michael Downey, born 27 January 1951, Dublin; grew up in Crumlin; his father played in a pipe band and loved jazz; school bands the Liffey Beats, Mod Con Cave Dwellers, the Black Eagles (with Lynott), then Sugar Shack and Orphanage; Thin Lizzy founder; with Lynott the only constant member to 1983; reunions 1996 on and 2010-2013; Gary Moore's Close As You Get (2007); Brian Downey's Alive and Dangerous from 2016; Eduardo Rivadavia (AllMusic, Bad Reputation review): 'certainly one of the most underrated [rock drummers] of his generation'.

title: Thin Lizzy - Wikipedia
notes: Read to character 100,000 of 167,712. Bell saw Downey and Lynott with Orphanage in December 1969; Downey agreed to a new band if Lynott played bass; founders Lynott, Bell, Downey and Eric Wrixon; Downey quit and returned mid-tour in Germany, 1974; pneumonia in 1978, Mark Nauseef deputised; Nauseef and Mike Mesbur deputised in 1982; farewell tour 1983; Self Aid 1986; Tommy Aldridge filled in from 1997, then took the chair; Downey back 2010; Scott Travis in 2016; Visconti's claim that only the drums and audience on Live and Dangerous were not overdubbed; twin lead guitars from 1974.

title: Peter Murphy, 'Keeping Himself Lizzy', Hot Press, 7 February 2011
notes: Reprinted 27 January 2025 (https://www.hotpress.com/music/happy-birthday-brian-downey-revisiting-a-classic-hot-press-interview-23067116). Intro: 'Delicate and light-fingered on ballads like Still In Love With You', 'economic and precise on Waiting For An Alibi and Jailbreak', 'an exquisite swing, tossing deft, almost jazzy fills'. Downey: 'I love Elvin Jones and Max Roach. And you have to include Buddy Rich. In the rock thing Billy Cobham and Vinnie Colaiuta'; Neil Peart 'a superb drummer'; father in the Harold's Cross Pipe Band, lessons with the Fintan Lawlor Pipe Band; on Lynott, 'nearly impossible for it to become complicated', 'a minimalist's discipline', 'his right hand was very strict', the rhythm section 'second to none'; ''Bad Reputation' has that weird time signature, and I like playing 'Emerald''; Sha-La-La improvised, 'four or five new patterns after eight or sixteen bars'; 'I like a ring' (toms); Visconti and Good Earth; congas and timpani; rudiments (single stroke roll, the long roll, double and triple paradiddles, triplets, ratamacues); 2011 kit: Tama Starclassic, two 22-inch bass drums, 14x5.5 snare, 13-inch Zildjian K hi-hats, K ride, crashes, china, splash; Wincent 5B.

title: Will Russell, 'Brian Downey on Thin Lizzy and Vagabonds of the Western World: Nobody could really label us', Hot Press, 11 January 2024
notes: Playing since 8 or 9; pipe band, father a drummer; the Liffey Beats, Mod Con Cave Dwellers, the Black Eagles, Sugar Shack, Orphanage (Lynott, Downey, Terry Woods, Joe Staunton, Pat Quigley); 'We were mainly a blues band'; Elvis, Gene Vincent, Bill Haley, then the Beatles; the first album in five days; Shades 'just didn't gel'; Vagabonds rehearsed; Ted Carroll heard them jamming Whiskey in the Jar; Dick Rowe wanted it as the A-side; The Rocker 'in Thin Lizzy's set until we finished'.

title: Modern Drummer, 'Brian Downey: Style, Power, And Swing With Thin Lizzy', 9 March 2011
notes: No byline. 'explosive chops, a fine sense of dynamics', 'one of the sweetest grooves in heavy rock'; The Boys Are Back in Town 'an unstoppable uptempo shuffle groove'; Emerald, Cowboy Song, Sha-La-La (Live and Dangerous) and Roisin Dubh as high points; his father an Irish pipe band drummer who passed on Eddie 'Cleanhead' Vinson and Oscar Brown Jr. The article dates The Boys Are Back in Town 1977; the single is 1976.

title: Mike Dolbear, 'Brian Downey' (British Drum Icons), interviewed January 2007 at SARM Studios
notes: Posted 31 March 2017; the interview is from the last day of Gary Moore's Close As You Get sessions (January 2007). Eddie 'Cleanhead' Vinson's Back Door Blues with Louis Hayes ('really intricate, but very fresh'); Oscar Brown Jr's When I Was Cool, 'a real sort of blues shuffle thing which was very influential'; pipe band from about 9; Tony Meehan of the Shadows (See You in My Drums); Ringo's backbeat; first kit an Olympic (bass drum, snare, hi-hat, no ride, 'it gave me a sort of independence'); then Premier; Hayman by the third or fourth Lizzy gig; Gretsch with 'a pair of big 26" bass drums' on Nightlife and Fighting; then Rogers (double bass drums, 12, 13, 14, 16), rewrapped chrome by Chas Foote; later Tama, including Cobham's Superstar; Zyn, Super Zyn, Paiste, then Zildjian; Lynott: 'you play with brushes'; 'influenced by Deep Purple and Hendrix'; Whiskey in the Jar meant as a B-side to Black Boys on the Corner; Yamaha Absolutes and a maple snare (2007); admires Brian Blade.

title: OnlineDrummer: The Boys Are Back in Town (Steve Ley), product description
notes: The description only; the PDF was not read. 'a rockin' shuffle-groove throughout, punctuating the guitarists' riffs with off-beat hi-hat slurps and end-of-the-bar crashes'; album version (4:29); level 3 of 4.

title: Colin Hunt, Brian Downey's Alive and Dangerous live review, Über Rock, 12 February 2019
notes: 'one of the world's most underrated rock drummers'; the Sha La La solo played live.

title: Thin Lizzy (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded 4-9 January 1971 at Decca Studios; released 30 April 1971; The Friendly Ranger at Clontarf Castle (Bell, Lynott); Downey co-wrote Return of the Farmer's Son; long days, nine in the morning to eight or nine at night.

title: Whiskey in the Jar - Wikipedia
notes: Thin Lizzy single, Decca, 3 November 1972; recorded 23-25 September 1972 at Decca; arranged by Bell, Downey and Lynott; No. 1 in Ireland, No. 6 UK; B-side Black Boys on the Corner; Metallica's version 1998 (Garage Inc.).

title: Vagabonds of the Western World - Wikipedia
notes: Released 21 September 1973; AIR and Decca, April to July 1973; The Rocker (Bell, Downey, Lynott), Slow Blues (Downey, Lynott), Little Girl in Bloom (Lynott); Whiskey in the Jar on the 1991 CD.

title: Fighting (Thin Lizzy album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 12 September 1975; Olympic Studios, May 1975; produced by Lynott; Wild One (Lynott); Downey co-wrote For Those Who Love to Live.

title: Jailbreak (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 26 March 1976; Ramport Studios, December 1975 to February 1976; John Alcock; Cowboy Song (Downey, Lynott); Emerald (Gorham, Robertson, Downey, Lynott); The Boys Are Back in Town single 17 April 1976.

title: Johnny the Fox - Wikipedia
notes: Released 16 October 1976; Musicland abandoned, finished at Ramport and Olympic; trouble getting a drum sound; Don't Believe a Word: Downey 'devised a faster shuffle rhythm' when he and Robertson reworked Lynott's slow 12-bar blues; Gorham on Johnny the Fox Meets Jimmy the Weed: 'took off when Brian Downey sat down and put his personal funk take on it with the drums'; Phil Collins on percussion, track unknown.

title: Bad Reputation (Thin Lizzy album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 2 September 1977; Toronto Sound and Sounds Interchange, May-June 1977; Visconti; Bad Reputation and Opium Trail co-written by Downey; Dancing in the Moonlight (Lynott), UK No. 14.

title: Live and Dangerous - Wikipedia
notes: Released 2 June 1978; Hammersmith Odeon 14 November 1976, Tower Theater Philadelphia October 1977, Seneca College Toronto 28 October 1977, overdubs in Paris January 1978; Visconti: '75% recorded in the studio', the drums and audience from the live tapes; the 2022 box showed far less overdubbing; Sha La La on side four.

title: Black Rose: A Rock Legend - Wikipedia
notes: Released 13 April 1979; Pathé Marconi (Paris), Good Earth and Morgan (London); Visconti; Gary Moore; Do Anything You Want To (Lynott); S & M (Downey, Lynott); Mark Nauseef uncredited on Sarah.

title: Chinatown (Thin Lizzy album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 10 October 1980; Good Earth then RAK, April-August 1980; Kit Woolven; Snowy White, Darren Wharton; Chinatown (Downey, Gorham, Lynott, White); on Chinatown Downey 'added double bass drum fills'.
